headline: Island Docking and Mainland Entry Requirements
reservation: The park consists of several mainland bases and over 20 islands. While mainland areas require a standard entry pass, docking or camping on islands requires a specific permit and fee. During peak summer, island campsites must be booked via the national reservation service; always verify current docking availability on the official website before departing from the marina.

days.title: River Views and Shoreline Exploration

stops.name: Mallorytown Landing
stops.detail: Visit the park's primary mainland hub to view the aquarium and interpretative exhibits about the St. Lawrence ecosystem.

stops.name: Jones Creek
stops.detail: Hike the trail network through various wetland habitats and look for local wildlife from the boardwalk overlooks.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for mainland travel; conditions vary.
days.note: Mainland trails can be buggy in early summer; check local reports for tick prevalence in tall grass areas.

days.title: Island Hopping and River History

stops.name: Beaurivage Island
stops.detail: Accessible only by boat, this island offers scenic picnic spots and a glimpse into the historic 'Gilded Age' cottage culture.

stops.name: McDonald Island
stops.detail: Explore the rugged granite shorelines and pitch-pine ridges that define the Frontenac Arch Biosphere.

days.driving: Local water transfer only; allow 30-60 minutes for boat transit.
days.note: Verify current weather and river currents before setting out in small craft like kayaks or canoes.

days.title: Panoramic Perspectives and Rockport

stops.name: Landon Bay
stops.detail: Hike to the 'Lookout' trail for one of the most famous views of the St. Lawrence River and the surrounding archipelago.

stops.name: Heaths Point
stops.detail: Observe the unique geology where the Canadian Shield crosses the river into the United States.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes between mainland points; conditions vary.
days.note: Landon Bay is popular for birdwatching; bring binoculars for spotting ospreys or bald eagles near the river.

intel.title: Mainland Hubs
intel.text: Parking at Mallorytown Landing is organized but fills quickly on holiday weekends. Smaller trailheads like Jones Creek have limited roadside capacity.

intel.title: Border Roaming
intel.text: Due to proximity to the US border, mobile devices often ping international towers. Check your data plan to avoid accidental roaming charges while on the river.

intel.title: Marine and Road Supplies
intel.text: Roadside fuel is available in Gananoque and Brockville. Boat fuel is only available at private marinas in gateway towns, not on the national park islands.

intel.title: Water Access Window
intel.text: Island docks are typically installed in late May and removed by mid-October. Off-season island access is possible but limited by river ice and weather.

intel.title: Boat Dependent Navigation
intel.text: The majority of the park is inaccessible by car. Visitors without a personal vessel should book commercial cruises or rentals in Gananoque or Rockport.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Ottawa (YOW), rent a car, and drive south to the Thousand Islands Parkway. Check into accommodation in Gananoque for easy marina access.
plan.vehicle: A car is necessary for mainland trails, but a boat (private or rental) is the only way to experience the island-based park features.
plan.goldenHour: The Landon Bay Lookout provides an elevated southern perspective ideal for watching the river light change during late summer afternoons.
